body.statement: For every member of \(\mathfrak M\) there is a common \(G_{\infty}\in C^3(\mathcal K;\mathbb S_{+}^{Fp})\) such that, for every balanced \(m=m(n)\) with \(m\to\infty\), \(N\to\infty\), and \(m/n\to0\), \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_n^{\mathrm{full}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\to0,\] and \[\max_{0\le j\le3}\sup_{\beta\in\mathcal K}\lVert D_{\rho}^{j}G_{T_{n,m}^{\mathrm{main}}}(\beta)-D_{\rho}^{j}G_{\infty}(\beta)\rVert\xrightarrow{P_{S_m}}0.\] Here \(D_{\rho}^{0}G=G\), the first display is deterministic conditional on the complete baseline array, and the second probability is over the uniform pilot split conditional on that array.
body.justification: The common experiment-indexed limit removes ambiguity about which empirical oracle and which convergence mode define the boundary constants.
body.gap: First-order learned-rerandomization arguments require consistency of one selected score, whereas the second-order boundary expansion needs uniform convergence of the oracle map and its first three quotient derivatives along both realized experiment sequences.
body.consumer: It gives replication planners one stable limiting geometry whether the oracle is evaluated on all registered units or on the random main-wave complement.

obligation.what_is_open: Uniform convergence of the empirical oracle and its first three quotient derivatives along both the full array and every vanishing random complement.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen conditional-moment smoothness is imposed only on the support of the limiting baseline measure. It does not control moment values at actual off-support triangular-array points, so weak empirical convergence alone cannot justify passage of empirical moments to their limits.
obligation.attempted: Expanded the oracle into empirical conditional first and second moments, then tried weak-convergence and deletion bounds. The weak-convergence step fails at off-support array points; a common-compact continuity condition is proposed.
obligation.partial_result: Under the proposed common-compact moment condition, weak convergence of the empirical baseline measures implies uniform convergence of every bounded continuous empirical moment entering \(\mathcal B_T\), together with its first three \(\rho\)-derivatives.  Deleting \(m=o(n)\) bounded summands changes each such moment by \(O(m/n)\), uniformly in the realized split.  The remaining step is to propagate these convergences through the covariance pseudoinverse and trace normalization on the stated constant-rank stratum.
